State the rule: this is the Doppler effect. The source moves while emitting, so wavefronts pile up ahead of the motion and spread out behind it. Here the source is moving to the left, toward X and away from Y.
For a stationary observer, wave speed $v$ is unchanged but observed wavelength $\lambda_{o}$ is changed, with observed frequency $f_{o} = v/\lambda_{o}$.
At X the observed wavelength is shortened by the source motion, so $\lambda_{X} < v/F$ and $f_{X} = v/\lambda_{X} > F$.
At Y the observed wavelength is lengthened by the source motion, so $\lambda_{Y} > v/F$ and $f_{Y} = v/\lambda_{Y} < F$.
The combination $>F$ at X and $<F$ at Y matches the row with $>F$ then $<F$. This is option C.
